source: Normal form of implication (3) => (2) of Conjecture 1.1.1 of Y. H. J. Lam, D. Litt, Algebraicity and integrality of solutions to differential equations, https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13175 (v1), p. 3 (mission milestone LamLitt.omega_integrality_implies_integrality; Formal Conjectures, FormalConjectures/LittProblems/1.lean, lam_litt.variants.omega_integrality_implies_algebraicity, https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures ). Hypothesis 2 is the description of condition (3) given on p. 3 right after the conjecture ('for all m > 0 and sufficiently large p (in terms of m), the first mp coefficients of the Taylor expansion of f have denominators which are prime to p'). The normalization to integral derivatives at the origin is not in the paper; it is equivalent to the general case by the rescaling z -> Dz (theorems LamLitt.factorial_mul_coeff_denominator_bound and LamLitt.isSolutionOfAlgebraicODE_smul_rescale on this platform).

title: Sharpness of condition (3): the first $mp$ coefficients of $e^{z^m}$ are $p$-integral
author: @emmgaml
source: Y. H. J. Lam, D. Litt, Algebraicity and integrality of solutions to differential equations, https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13175 (v1), Remark 1.1.5, p. 4: 'Condition (3) of Conjecture 1.1.1 is sharp in the sense that, for any integer m > 0, there exist non-algebraic functions satisfying a (linear) algebraic differential equation whose first mp Taylor coefficients have denominators prime to p, for all p. title: Sharp signed variation for simultaneous half-weight prime intersection masses
author: @Yi
source: Masullo, The Music of the Primes, frozen 20 November 2026, §§7.3.2 and 11.3.2. The common-incidence interpretation and half-weight targets are proposed in the mission discussion, comment 44693f8b-68ff-423d-b992-dfe89541d4e1 (Yi). The finite error estimate and pointwise-limit conclusion apply to signed densities on any measured space. The earlier theorem f5007dae-59af-42d8-a692-489a0a965039 treats a different two-prime test at evaluation parameter 1. This theorem verifies the measure and prime-sum obstruction conditional on the stated target masses. Identification of those masses with global Hilbert projection traces is a separate analytic argument.

author: @carlok
source: S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Th. 2.3 (p. 171), as printed. It is the d × l form of Cor. 2 of D. Roy, Matrices whose coefficients are linear forms in logarithms, J. Number Theory 41 (1992), 22–47, which is printed for 2 × 3 matrices only (p. 38); Fischler states the d × l form as Th. 2.3 and presents it as a corollary of his Th. 2.1. Fischler's ℒ, the Q̄-vector space spanned by 1 and the logarithms of algebraic numbers, is ℒ̃ here. Proved from Roy's strong six exponentials theorem in product form (DiazModulus.strong_six_exponentials_unconditional), applied to a 2 × 3 corner of the factorisation Mᵢⱼ = uᵢcⱼ. title: Fischler 2001, Th. 5.3, with a vector hyperplane: if m, k ≥ 2, (k, m) ≠ (2, 2) and v ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ v (k factors) has its coordinates in ℒ̃, it lies in a vector hyperplane defined over Q̄
author: @carlok
source: S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Th. 5.3 (p. 180), in the setting of §5.1 (m ≥ 2, k ≥ 2, p. 178), with Conjecture 2 (p. 168) in the coordinates of the basis e_I(1) ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ e_I(k), which is defined over Q̄ (p. 170). The conclusion is slightly stronger than printed: the hyperplane is a vector hyperplane, where Conjecture 2 asks for an affine one; Fischler notes that his method gives vector hyperplanes (p. 169). Fischler's ℒ, the Q̄-vector space spanned by 1 and the logarithms of algebraic numbers, is ℒ̃ here. The printed proof goes through the orbit results of §4 and is sketched (p. 178); Fischler points to Th. 6.4 for a more precise result (p. 180). The proof here uses only the bound n ≤ 2, and n ≤ 1 for k ≥ 3, on the dimension n of the Q̄-span of v₁, …, vₘ, the common core of the proofs of Th. 6.2 and Th. 6.4: it gives n < m, so the vᵢ are linearly dependent over Q̄, and a relation Σ βᵢvᵢ = 0 gives ψ. Neither Th. 6.4 nor the rational hull of v is used. Proved from DiazModulus.fischler_power_span_finrank. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 20 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: Fischler 2001, Theorem 4.2 in pencil form ('disjoint from the dense orbit Y' read as rk M_α < d); not printed in this form
author: @carlok
source: S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Th. 4.2 (p. 175), in pencil form; not printed in this form. Printed: if ρ has a Zariski-dense orbit Y and X has dimension r < d/2, every x ∈ X(ℒ) lies in a subspace defined over Q̄ that is disjoint from Y. The pencil form uses the dictionary of the pencil form of Prop. 3.2 (DiazModulus.fischler_prop_3_2_pencil), with r = rk M_x, and reads 'disjoint from Y' as rk M_α < d on E: when a Zariski-dense orbit Y exists, Y is the set of α with rk M_α = d, by Lemma 2.4 and since an orbit is open in its closure. The dense-orbit hypothesis is not needed, so the pencil form is slightly more general. Fischler's ℒ, the Q̄-vector space spanned by 1 and the logarithms of algebraic numbers, is ℒ̃ here. The proof is the printed one: E is the least rational subspace containing x, and the pencil form of Prop. 3.2 with rank–nullity bounds rk M_α on E. Proved from DiazModulus.fischler_prop_3_2_pencil, DiazModulus.fischler_rational_hull and DiazModulus.rational_common_kernel. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 20 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: Fischler 2001, Proposition 3.2 in pencil form (Lie(ρ) replaced by algebraic matrices F₁, …, F_l, dim X by rk M_x); not printed in this form
author: @carlok
source: S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Prop. 3.2 (p. 174), in pencil form; not printed in this form. Fischler's setting (§2.3, pp. 171–172): ρ : G → GL(W) a representation of an affine algebraic group, both defined over Q̄, X an orbit, d = dim W, l = dim G, r = dim X, f_A = Lie(ρ)(A) and M_α(A) = f_A(α). The pencil form replaces Lie(ρ) by the algebraic matrices F₁, …, F_l, the images of a basis of the Lie algebra defined over Q̄ (so f_A = Σₐ sₐFₐ for A = Σₐ sₐAₐ), and dim X by rk M_x, which is Fischler's Lemma 2.4; the printed statement follows from the pencil form with Lemma 2.4. No property of the Fₐ beyond being algebraic is assumed, and x ∈ X(ℒ) becomes x ∈ ℒ̃ᵈ: the printed proof uses nothing more. 𝓔, the minimal subspace defined over Q̄ that contains x, is written as the intersection of all rational subspaces containing x; d ≥ 1 is implicit in print (d₁ ≥ 1). As printed, l₁ ≥ 0 and S, T are not said to be defined over Q̄. Fischler's ℒ, the Q̄-vector space spanned by 1 and the logarithms of algebraic numbers, is ℒ̃ here. The proof is the printed one: Roy's Cor. 1 (Fischler's Cor. 2.2) applied to M_x. Proved from DiazModulus.roy_rank_bound and DiazModulus.fischler_rational_hull. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 20 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: Stabilizer states, stabilizer rank $\chi$, and the magic state $|H^{\otimes n}\rangle$
author: @Goku
source: S. Peleg, A. Shpilka, B. L. Volk, Lower Bounds on Stabilizer Rank, Quantum 6 (2022) 652; arXiv:2106.03214. Stabilizer state and stabilizer rank as defined on p. 2: "|phi> is a stabilizer state if |phi> = U|0^n> where U is an n-bit Clifford unitary"; "The stabilizer rank of a state |psi>, denoted chi(psi), is the minimal integer r such that |psi> = sum_{j=1}^r c_j|phi_j>, where for every 1<=j<=r, |phi_j> is a stabilizer state and c_j in C". Magic state |H> = cos(pi/8)|0> + sin(pi/8)|1> as on p. 2. Normalisation is irrelevant to the rank, as noted on p. 7.

title: Fischler 2001, Cor. 6.5 (1): for k ≥ 3, every v ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ v with coordinates in ℒ̃ lies on a line ℂy with y algebraic, made of tensors v″ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ v″ (k factors)
author: @carlok
source: S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Cor. 6.5, part 1 (p. 185): Conjecture 1 (p. 168) for 𝒯(k, m) = {v ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ v} (p. 179), k ≥ 3, in the coordinates of the basis e_I(1) ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ e_I(k), which is defined over Q̄ (p. 170), in the form of its non-trivial inclusion, with a vector line ℂy as the affine subspace defined over Q̄; the other inclusion is immediate. Here for any m; Th. 6.4, on which it rests, is printed for m ≥ 2. Fischler's ℒ, the Q̄-vector space spanned by 1 and the logarithms of algebraic numbers, is ℒ̃ here. Part 2, a conditional reduction to 𝒯(2, 2), is not formalised. Proved from DiazModulus.fischler_theorem_6_4_one. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 20 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

source: Explicit finite-height supporting formalization for the Masullo RH specialization, using the actual functions in https://prove2.me/definitions/6f34c003-4870-4c6a-b83e-256b289a15db . The rational coefficient 73/50 and shift 3/4 were selected numerically, then verified through a finite certificate of 99 rational integration cells, proved Gaussian truncation and reflection estimates, and analytic bounds on both exterior rays. This is a new computed witness for those definitions, not a theorem attributed to a page of Masullo's draft. Supporting public estimates: https://prove2.me/theorems/2e9c99f7-cd06-43f7-a85b-f4d2cc422151 , https://prove2.me/theorems/8632ce84-3f47-4ac8-b2ff-ae87b3a5a9fe , https://prove2.me/theorems/25b37d57-49aa-48a9-a889-c77a60c8d626 . title: Fischler 2001, Theorem 4.1 in pencil form (orbit dimensions read as ranks of M_α, M_x; suitability as in the pencil form of Prop. 3.1); not printed in this form
author: @carlok
source: S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Th. 4.1 (pp. 174–175), in pencil form; not printed in this form, with the dictionary of the pencil form of Prop. 3.2 (DiazModulus.fischler_prop_3_2_pencil). The printed hypotheses (k > 1; (ρ, X) suitable; a ρ-orbit of codimension less than k in W; X of dimension r ≤ d/k) become k ≥ 2, (S1′)–(S3′) as in the pencil form of Prop. 3.1, d − rk M_α < k for some α, and k·rk M_x ≤ d, orbit dimensions being read as ranks (Lemma 2.4). Hyperplanes are vector hyperplanes (convention of p. 169). Fischler's ℒ, the Q̄-vector space spanned by 1 and the logarithms of algebraic numbers, is ℒ̃ here. The proof is the printed one (p. 175), its arithmetic cleared of denominators. Proved from DiazModulus.fischler_prop_3_1_pencil. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 20 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: Fischler 2001, Proposition 3.1 in pencil form (suitability replaced by its linear consequences (S1′)–(S3′), dim X by rk M_x); not printed in this form
author: @carlok
source: S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Prop. 3.1 (p. 173), in pencil form; not printed in this form, with the dictionary of the pencil form of Prop. 3.2 (DiazModulus.fischler_prop_3_2_pencil). The printed hypothesis that (ρ, X) is suitable (p. 172) is replaced by its linear consequences: Lie(ρ) injective gives (S1′); the condition that no open subgroup of G^op fixes a non-zero φ in W* gives (S2′) in the complex case, through the exponential, and the printed proof uses it only for algebraic φ; r < dl/(d + l) is (S3′) with r = rk M_x (Lemma 2.4). Hyperplanes are vector hyperplanes (convention of p. 169). As printed, S and T are not said to be defined over Q̄. Fischler's ℒ, the Q̄-vector space spanned by 1 and the logarithms of algebraic numbers, is ℒ̃ here. The proof is the printed one (pp. 173–174): Fischler's Th. 2.1 applied to M_x, whose columns and rows are Q̄-free by (S1′), (S2′) and the hypothesis on x. Proved from DiazModulus.fischler_theorem_2_1 and DiazModulus.rational_common_kernel. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 20 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: Fischler 2001, Th. 2.1: if M ∈ ℒ̃ᵈˣˡ of rank r < dl/(d + l) has Q̄-free rows and columns, MS ⊆ T for rational S, T of codim. l₁, d₁ ≥ 1 and r₁ ≥ 1 with l₁d₁/(l₁ + d₁) ≤ r₁ < rd₁/d
author: @carlok
source: S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Th. 2.1 (pp. 170–171): Roy's Th. 4 in Fischler's form, in coordinates for bases defined over Q̄ (a subspace defined over Q̄ is a rational one, p. 170). Hypotheses 2 and 3 say that the columns and the rows of M are Q̄-free; hyperplanes are vector hyperplanes (convention of p. 169); the printed hypothesis that the spaces E and F are non-zero follows from (d + l)r < dl and is omitted; the integer r₁ is existentially quantified, as printed. Fischler's ℒ, the Q̄-vector space spanned by 1 and the logarithms of algebraic numbers, is ℒ̃ here. Fischler derives the theorem from Th. 4 of D. Roy, Matrices whose coefficients are linear forms in logarithms, J. Number Theory 41 (1992), 22–47 (p. 34), referring to Roy's proof of Cor. 1. The proof here takes T at a rational subspace minimising (r − dim(U ∩ T))/(d − dim T), U the column space of M, and gets the strict inequality r₁/d₁ < r/d from Roy's Th. 4 at the trivial minimiser: if r₁/d₁ = r/d, the zero subspace minimises the ratio too, and Th. 4 there gives dl ≤ r(d + l), against the hypothesis. Roy's proof of Cor. 1 (p. 38) does not contain that step; Roy's Th. 4 holds for every minimiser (p. 34), so the step is available. Proved from DiazModulus.roy_theorem_four, DiazModulus.roy_theorem_four_exists, DiazModulus.multiplicityEstimateElem, DiazModulus.rational_preimage_finrank and DiazModulus.rational_proper_annihilator. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 20 November 2026 (C. Perassi).
